opus-5.5.text:
Yeah, I think for me it comes down to a fairly simple belief: the things we learn from pushing a model on something really hard, like olympiad-level math, should flow back into the model that everyone actually uses. If you build a very bespoke, narrow system for one competition, you might get a great result, but it's kind of a dead end. You get a trophy, and then you have to ask what you've really learned that transfers.

With a single general-purpose model, the bet is different. You're saying the same model that helps someone write code, answer questions, or reason through a messy problem should also be able to sit down and produce a rigorous proof. If we can get there, it tells you something about the underlying capability, the reasoning, the ability to think for longer and verify your own steps, rather than just clever engineering around one domain.

I've always been a bit of a "generalist model" person. Historically, a lot of progress has come from unifying things that used to be separate specialized systems into one model that does it all. Every time we did that, the general model eventually caught up to and surpassed the specialists. Math felt like one of the last places where people assumed you'd need formal tools, specialized pipelines, and so on. Showing that a general model can operate there in natural language is a strong signal about where things are heading.

There's also a practical side. A general model is what reaches people. If the reasoning improvements we develop for something as demanding as the IMO live in the main model, then everybody benefits, not just a research demo. That's the direction I want AI to go: fewer one-off systems, more capable general systems that keep getting smarter across the board.

r001.rationale: The candidate says the same general-purpose model should handle coding, questions, messy problems, and rigorous proofs, and argues for fewer one-off systems.

r002.rationale: The candidate does not state that the IMO model was released essentially unchanged, and does not identify Gemini Deep Think.

fable-5.1.text:
Yeah, so I think the thing that mattered to me most about the IMO result wasn't actually the gold medal itself. It was that we got there with the same general model, basically Gemini Deep Think, rather than some bespoke system that only knows how to do olympiad math.

The way I see it, there have been two paths you could take. One is you build a narrow system, you hook it up to Lean or some formal verifier, you do a ton of search on top, and you engineer the whole pipeline around one benchmark. And that can work, and it's impressive in its own way. But to me it's kind of a dead end, because what you learn doesn't transfer. You've solved IMO, but you haven't really learned anything about intelligence.

The other path is you just make the model better at reasoning, generally, in natural language. You're not translating the problem into some formal system, you're not doing anything special. You give it the problem the way a human student would get it, and it writes a proof the way a human would write it. And if that works, then the same capability that got you the gold medal should also show up when you're doing research, or debugging code, or whatever else.

And that's the direction I actually care about. Like, I've always been more of a generalist in terms of taste. I don't find the narrow stuff that exciting, even when the numbers are good. What excites me is when one model gets better at a lot of things at once because the underlying reasoning got better. The IMO thing was nice because it was a very clean, very hard, very public test of exactly that.

Also, honestly, there's a practical angle. If you need a different model for every domain, you've basically recreated the pre-LLM world where everything was a special-purpose system. The whole point of this era is that you don't have to do that. So it would've felt a bit backwards to go win IMO with a thing that couldn't also answer your email.

r001.rationale: The response says the same general reasoning capability should apply across research, code debugging, and other domains, and argues that one model should handle many tasks.

r002.rationale: It identifies Gemini Deep Think as the general model used for the IMO result, but does not say that the IMO model was released essentially unchanged.

astra-6.text:
I think the goal is to build a model that can do many different things really well, and mathematics is one important part of that. We don’t want to build a system that’s only good at solving olympiad problems. We want the reasoning capabilities that help it solve those problems to also be useful when it’s writing code, doing science, or helping someone with a difficult question.

So using one general-purpose model is really consistent with that direction. The IMO is a way to test how far we can push its reasoning, but the broader question is whether that progress makes the model more capable in general. That’s the part I find exciting.

r001.rationale: It says the goal is one model that does many things well and explains that IMO reasoning should also help with coding, science, and difficult questions.

r002.rationale: It does not state that the IMO model was released essentially unchanged as Gemini Deep Think.

sol-6.1.text:
I think the goal is to build a model that can learn to solve many different kinds of problems. Math is a really good test of that because you have to reason through something difficult, and there’s a fairly clear notion of whether you got it right. But we want those capabilities to carry over to coding, science, and other tasks as well.

So, for me, the exciting question is whether the IMO can be a milestone on the path toward a more general model. If we improve a general-purpose model enough that it can solve these problems, while still being useful across other domains, that feels much closer to the direction we want AI to take.

r001.rationale: It says the aim is a general model that solves many kinds of problems and carries capabilities across coding, science, and other tasks, linking the IMO effort to broad general-purpose capability.

r002.rationale: It does not say the IMO model was released as Gemini Deep Think or that it was released essentially unchanged.
